span.p:
22 GB real Thai call-centre audio (D97)
outside the repo, gitignored - the transcripts
have names and account numbers in them.
Their noise spans are ground truth for the
endpointer, which CER cannot measure.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ports/vad.py — the 9th port (D96)
returns a PROBABILITY, not a decision

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
endpointer.py — NO model, NO I/O, NO clock
D9's constants live here and are assertable:
0.65 threshold · 500ms speech · 100ms silence
120ms pad BEFORE — the first syllable carries the tone

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
level gate (B14)
is there any energy in this segment?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
stream.py: one consumer, one seq counter
ingestion NEVER waits for the model

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the ring buffer OWES audio to every queued segment (B20).
It used to release it 30s behind the NEWEST segment, so when
the model fell behind, the early sentences were gone before
it saw them - and _slice CLAMPED, handing back the wrong
moment at the right length rather than nothing at all.

span.p:
EnergyVad — no dependencies.
The CI path AND the degradation rung

span.p:
SileroVad — from the PACKAGE,

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: ScriptedSttEngine — every test, the stage-safe path

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
TyphoonAsr - THE ENGINE (D104). A NeMo transducer,
so NO 30s window: p95 0.19s, 20 of 20 calls inside
the 1.5s budget. Nothing else has ever met it.
Fed silence it returns EMPTY in 149ms, where Whisper
spends 8578ms inventing Thai (B14 vs D99).

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
FasterWhisper CT2 int8_float16 - THE FALLBACK (D103),
for a box where NeMo will not install. Needs the hint:
without it int8 costs 0.109 -> 0.171 CER (B19).
ThonburianHf fp16 - the original, 19.5s p95. Too slow.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
THREE guards, three DIFFERENT KINDS — none optional
1. a repeated chunk burying the sentence? (B16: the first
version split on spaces and caught 0 of 3 REAL Thai loops)
2. mostly OUR OWN vocabulary handed back? (B14)
3. more speech than physically possible? (D98: real Thai is
median 7.6 chars/s, max 15; the real loops are 39-53)
DIGITS ARE EXEMPT from guard 1 (B21): a real Thai phone
number has FIVE identical digit words in a row, and the
guard was deleting them in 9 of 12 calls.
The guards STAY under Typhoon even though it does not
hallucinate on silence - they are the degradation path
back to the CT2 fallback, and cost microseconds.
